exposure: Opioid prescribing after vaginal or cesarean delivery
Size of opioid prescription in oral morphine equivalents
cohort: 988,036 opioid-naïve women with continuous insurance coverage for 1 year before and after delivery from a single private payer
finding: While both opioid prescribing and new persistent opioid use after delivery decreased from 2008 to 2016, modifiable prescribing patterns were associated with persistent opioid use after vaginal delivery, and risk factors for persistent use after cesarean delivery mirrored those of other surgical conditions.
mod_finding: Opioid prescription fills decreased for both vaginal and cesarean deliveries, with fewer women experiencing new persistent opioid use in both groups.
